Added ⚠ PII leak-path warnings to Session.username and AccountInfo.name rustdocs enumerating Display, tracing %, Serialize, and similar accidental-leak paths. description:
request.rs:116 — pub username: String
request.rs:244 — pub name: String (on AccountInfo)

Both fields contain PII (typically email addresses, RFC 8620 §2). The Debug impls correctly redact them (bd:JMAP-sc1b.99 / .104). But the fields are `pub String` — meaning callers who write:

  println!("User: {}", session.username);          // Display, not redacted
  format!("Account: {}", account.name);             // Display, not redacted
  serde_json::to_string(&session)?;                 // Serialize re-emits the raw value
  log::info!("session has username {}", session.username);  // Display path

…silently leak. The Debug redaction only catches `{:?}`-format paths. Any Display, any to_string(), any explicit serialize, leaks the PII verbatim.

The same defense-in-depth tripwire test pattern documented in workspace AGENTS.md ("Security testing" section) covers Debug-via-tracing-?, but does NOT cover:
- format!("{}", session.username)
- session.username.to_string() passed to log::info!
- to_string()-equivalent paths like println!("{}", value)
- serde_json::to_value(&session) (which round-trips the raw field)

For a public-API foundation client, the correct shape would be:
  pub username: Username  // a newtype wrapping String

…with a manual Display impl that redacts unless an explicit `.expose_unredacted()` method is called. The current `pub String` design forces the caller to know which fields are PII, which they will not — until a CI log surfaces the leak.

Defense-in-depth recommendation:
1. Add unit tests that exercise format!("{}", session.username) and assert the canary is present (positive control) — the test documents "if you write this code, you are leaking PII; the helper to redact is X".
2. Add a doc-warning on Session.username and AccountInfo.name pointing callers at the redacting accessor pattern.
3. Future minor: introduce a Username newtype for these two fields, with manual Display that redacts to "<user>@..." or similar.

The Debug-only redaction is half a solution. The other half is preventing accidental Display.
title: Session.username and AccountInfo.name are pub String fields — PII leak via accidental Display/serialize
